question.worked_solution:
We note that $x=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined.

The equation has the denominators $x$ and $3x.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(x,3x)=3x.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $3x,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x\cdot (\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{x}) & =3x\cdot (\frac{3-x}{3x}) \\ 3x\cdot \frac{2}{3}+3x\cdot \frac{1}{x} & =3x\cdot \frac{3-x}{3x} \\ \cancel{3}x\cdot \frac{2}{\cancel{3}}+3\cancel{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{x}} & =\cancel{3x}\cdot \frac{3-x}{\cancel{3x}} \\ x\cdot (2)+3\cdot (1) & =3-x \\ 2x+3 & =3-x\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $x,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =3-x \\ 2x+x & =3-3 \\ 3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $x=0$ as a solution. Since $x=0,$ we conclude that there is no solution.
